learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and understanding of engineering disciplines specific to their specialization, at the level necessary to acquire the rest of the degree competencies, including notions of the latest advances.
Awareness of the multidisciplinary context of engineering.

The ability to analyze complex products, processes, and systems in their field of study; to appropriately choose and apply established analytical, computational, and experimental methods and correctly interpret the results of such analyses.

The ability to identify, formulate, and solve engineering problems in their specialty; to appropriately choose and apply established analytical, computational, and experimental methods; to recognize the importance of social, health and safety, environmental, economic, and industrial constraints.

Ability to plan, design, and develop complex products (parts, components, finished products, etc.), processes, and systems in their specialty, that meet established requirements, including awareness of social, health and safety, environmental, economic, and industrial aspects; as well as to select and apply appropriate project methods.
Understanding of applicable techniques and methods of analysis, design, and research and their limitations in their specialty.
Knowledge of the application of materials, equipment and tools, technology, and engineering processes and their limitations in their specialty.
Ability to manage complex technical or professional activities or projects in their specialty, taking responsibility for decision-making.
Ability to effectively communicate information, ideas, problems, and solutions in the field of engineering and with society in general.
Ability to function effectively in national and international contexts, individually and in teams, and cooperate with both engineers and people from other disciplines.
Makes decisions and assesses the possible consequences of the selected alternative.
Identify the properties of fluids and analyze their hydrostatic behavior, and know the methods of analysis of fluid statics in both theoretical and practical environments.
Defines the problem, the development of the solution, as well as the conclusions effectively, and using correct language, in writing.
Analyze the hydrodynamic behavior of viscous fluids. Know the method of dimensional analysis and the theory of models, and apply them to different theoretical and practical environments.
Defines the problem, the development of the solution, as well as the conclusions effectively, and using correct language orally.
Coordinates their work with other team members, contributes to the development of tasks within their team, and creates a good working environment.

teaching_methods: Project-based learning (POPBLs), including report writing and presentations (individual and team)
Lectures and participatory classes covering concepts and procedures
Problem-solving and practical exercises (individual and team)

assessment_methods.method: Technical capacity, involvement in project/PBL, work performed, results obtained, documentation submitted, presentation and technical defense
Written and oral individual tests for the evaluation of technical competencies
Observation of student participation and attitude in training activities

assessment_rules: For project-based evaluations, assessment is continuous, based on team meetings with tutors and experts. A review is conducted a week before final submission to identify improvements, and the corrected final report serves as recovery. For evaluations involving written and oral individual tests, the recovery mechanism involves repeating these tests. If necessary, these tests may be conducted remotely.
